templates.tagline: Instant REST and GraphQL API with a no-code admin app for any SQL database

ADMIN_EMAIL.description: Email of the first admin user — you sign in with it.

templates.readme:
# Directus

Turns a SQL database into an instant REST and GraphQL API, with a no-code app
to manage content, users, files and permissions.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Directus** | `directus/directus:12.5.0` | Public. Admin app at `/admin`. 1 GiB volume for uploaded files |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Your data model and content |

## After deploy

Open `<your-url>/admin` and sign in with the **admin email and password** from
the deploy form.

## Notes

Directus uses the Business Source License: it is free for organizations under
USD 5M in annual revenue. Check [their license](https://directus.io/bsl) for
anything beyond that.

templates.name: Flowise
templates.tagline: Build AI agents and LLM workflows visually
templates.readme:
# Flowise

Build AI agents, chatbots and RAG pipelines with drag-and-drop nodes for every
major LLM, vector store and tool, then call them over an API or embed them on a
site.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Flowise** | `flowiseai/flowise:3.1.4` | Public. 1 GiB volume for uploaded documents and logs |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Chatflows, credentials and users |

The secrets Flowise uses to sign sessions and encrypt stored API keys are
generated for you.

## After deploy

Open the URL and create the **admin account**. The first visitor gets it.
Then add your model provider's API key under **Credentials**.

## Notes

On this release a few node types (the ReAct agent nodes and AWS Bedrock) fail to
load because of upstream packaging issues. Every other node works.

templates.readme:
# Ghost

A professional publishing platform: a modern editor, newsletters, paid
memberships and themes.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Ghost** | `ghost:6.70.0` | Public. 1 GiB volume for themes, images and uploads |
| **db** | MySQL 8 | Internal. Posts, members and settings |

## After deploy

Go to `<your-url>/ghost` and create the **owner account**. The first visitor to
that page gets it, so do this right away.

## Notes

- **Email.** Staff invites, password resets and newsletters need an SMTP or
  Mailgun account. Ghost reads its config from lowercase variables, so add yours
  to the `export …` line of the service's start command, e.g.
  `mail__transport=SMTP mail__options__host=…`.
- **Custom domain.** Ghost builds every link from its `url`. After you add a
  domain, set `GHOST_URL` to it and redeploy.

templates.readme:
# Miniflux

A minimalist, fast feed reader: RSS, Atom and JSON Feed, keyboard shortcuts,
full-text fetching, and a REST API, with no tracking and no clutter.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Miniflux** | `miniflux/miniflux:2.3.3` | Public. Migrations run on boot |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Feeds, entries and users |

## After deploy

Sign in with the **admin username and password** you entered in the deploy
form. Add more users under **Settings → Users**.

To use a mobile or desktop client (Fever or Google Reader API), enable it under
**Settings → Integrations**.

templates.readme:
# n8n

Workflow automation you host yourself: connect 400+ apps and APIs, run code
steps, and build AI agents on a visual canvas.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **n8n** | `n8nio/n8n:2.44.1` | Public. Editor, webhooks and the API on one URL. 1 GiB volume for credentials files and community nodes |
| **db** | PostgreSQL 16 | Internal. Workflows, executions and users |

`N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is generated for you. Every credential n8n stores is
encrypted with it, so **don't change or delete it**. If you lose it, the stored
credentials become unreadable.

## After deploy

1. Open the service URL. n8n asks you to create the **owner account**, and the
   first person to open the URL gets it, so do this right away.
2. Webhook URLs already point at the public address (`WEBHOOK_URL`). If you
   add a custom domain, update `WEBHOOK_URL` and `N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL` to match.

## Notes

- Schedule and polling triggers run inside the n8n process, so keep the
  service running if you rely on them.
- Large workflows can need more memory. Raise the limit in the service's
  **Scale** tab.

templates.name: Uptime Kuma
templates.tagline: Self-hosted uptime monitoring with status pages and alerts
templates.readme:
# Uptime Kuma

A friendly self-hosted monitoring tool. It checks HTTP(s), TCP, ping, DNS,
Docker and more, can publish public status pages, and sends alerts to 90+
notification services.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Uptime Kuma** | `louislam/uptime-kuma:2.5.6` | Public. 1 GiB volume for its database and settings |

## After deploy

1. Open the URL. On first launch Uptime Kuma asks which database to use: pick
   **SQLite**. It lives on the service's volume.
2. Create the admin account. The first visitor gets it, so do this right away.
3. Add monitors, then share a status page if you want one.

## Notes

Uptime Kuma checks from inside the platform, so keep the service running for
your monitors to keep firing.

templates.readme:
# Vaultwarden

A lightweight server that speaks the Bitwarden API, so the official Bitwarden
apps, browser extensions and CLI work against it.

## What gets deployed

| Service | Image | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Vaultwarden** | `vaultwarden/server:1.37.4` | Public. 1 GiB volume for the vault database (SQLite), attachments and keys |

## After deploy

1. Open the URL and **create your account**.
2. Turn off public signups: set `SIGNUPS_ALLOWED` to `false` in the service's
   variables and redeploy.
3. In any Bitwarden app, pick **Self-hosted** and enter the service URL as the
   server.

The admin panel lives at `/admin`, behind the `ADMIN_TOKEN` you chose at
deploy. Service variables are write-only, so keep a copy: to change it, set a
new `ADMIN_TOKEN` and redeploy. Deleting the variable turns the panel off.

## Notes

Vaultwarden is an independent project, not affiliated with Bitwarden, Inc.
Back up the volume: it is your vault.
